summary: All 8 acceptance-matrix criteria exercised: 8 browser checks + 3 backend test files (6 tests), all passing.

checks.name: student-signup-via-ui
checks.evidence: Registered tscheck-student-<ts>@example.com via /register (student tab), landed on /student/dashboard, heading visible, nav shows first name 'TSCheck' + Log out button.

checks.name: employer-signup-via-ui
checks.evidence: Registered employer with company 'TSCheck Co <ts>' via /register (employer tab), landed on /employer/dashboard; heading = company name; stats published/drafts/applicants all '0'.

checks.name: signup-validation-rejects-bad-input
checks.evidence: Duplicate email re-register showed 'already exists' toast and stayed on /register (backend 409 seen in console); employer submit with blank company blocked by HTML5 required validation (checkValidity()==false); password 'abc' blocked by minLength=6 validation, stayed on /register.

checks.name: test_tscheck_signup_validation.py
checks.evidence: POST /auth/register duplicate email -> 409 'An account with this email already exists'; POST /auth/register employer with company_name='' -> 422, and subsequent login for that email -> 401 (no account created).

checks.name: login-with-demo-accounts
checks.evidence: Demo student button prefilled student@dutchvacancy.nl, login -> /student/dashboard with stat-applications=3, stat-saved=2. Demo employer button prefilled employer@picnic.nl, login -> /employer/dashboard with stat-published=8 and applicants tab list visible.

checks.name: wrong-credentials-shows-error
checks.evidence: Login with student@dutchvacancy.nl + wrong password -> toast 'Invalid email or password' visible, stayed on /login, anonymous nav-login-link still present. Backend 401 observed in console (expected).

checks.name: test_tscheck_wrong_credentials.py
checks.evidence: POST /auth/login with wrong password -> 401 'Invalid email or password'; correct password for same account -> 200 with matching email.

checks.name: session-persists-and-logout-guards-dashboards
checks.evidence: After signup + full page reload, still on /student/dashboard with logout button visible. Logout -> redirected to '/', anonymous (login link visible). Direct nav to /student/dashboard and /employer/dashboard both redirect to /login.

checks.name: role-separation-redirects-and-anonymous-apply
checks.evidence: Student visiting /employer/dashboard redirected to /student/dashboard; employer visiting /student/dashboard redirected to /employer/dashboard; anonymous visitor clicking Apply on a job detail page got a 'log in' error toast and apply-dialog stayed hidden.

checks.name: test_tscheck_role_separation.py
checks.evidence: Logged-in student GET /employer/jobs -> 403; logged-in employer GET /student/applications -> 403 (session cookie forwarded explicitly per httpx localhost cookiejar note in test file docstring).

checks.name: auth-works-in-dutch
checks.evidence: Switched to NL on /login: submit button and h1 show 'Inloggen'; /register login-link shows 'Inloggen'; demo-student login in NL succeeded and landed on /student/dashboard.

notes: Matrix has 8 criteria; 2 of them (signup validation, role separation) are covered by both a browser check and a backend test file, yielding 11 total check artifacts.

Backend tests use an explicit Cookie header instead of relying on the httpx client's automatic cookie jar, because http.cookiejar (which httpx wraps) special-cases the bare host 'localhost' and drops cookies marked Secure sent over plain http — a test-tooling quirk, not an application bug. Real browsers treat localhost as a secure context, which is why the browser checks work fine with the default cookie flow.
seed.py was re-run once at the start of this iteration to ensure demo-account data matched the briefing's seed_facts (idempotent, as documented).
